title: Trading Stats
lessons/trading-system-u2-l1/steps/0/bod: **Win rate** is the percentage of your trades that were profitable. Alongside it, you have the **average win** of your winners and the **average loss** of your losers. None of them alone tells you whether a system makes money.
lessons/trading-system-u2-l1/steps/1/bod: **Expectancy** tells you what each trade is worth on average: **(win rate × average win) − (loss rate × average loss)**. If it's positive, the system has an **edge** over the long run.
lessons/trading-system-u2-l1/steps/2/pro: Win rate is 50%, the average win is $150 and the average loss is $100. What's the expectancy per trade?
lessons/trading-system-u2-l1/steps/2/exp: (0.5 × 150) − (0.5 × 100) = 75 − 50 = +$25. So on average, each trade adds $25 to the account.
lessons/trading-system-u2-l1/steps/3/pro: You have a system with a 70% win rate, a $50 average win and a $150 average loss. What's the expectancy per trade?
lessons/trading-system-u2-l1/steps/3/exp: (0.7 × 50) − (0.3 × 150) = 35 − 45 = −$10. Even though 7 out of 10 trades win, the system loses money over the long run.
lessons/trading-system-u2-l1/steps/4/sta: A high win rate means a system is definitely profitable.
lessons/trading-system-u2-l1/steps/4/exp: The last system won 70% of the time but lost money, because its losses were three times its wins. Always look at win rate alongside the size of wins and losses.
lessons/trading-system-u2-l1/steps/5/bod: You can measure everything in **R** (your risk on one trade): every loss is 1R and every win is, say, 2R. With a 40% win rate: 0.4 × 2 − 0.6 × 1 = **+0.2R**. So with $100 of risk, each trade is worth $20 on average.
lessons/trading-system-u2-l1/steps/5/tip: Breakeven win rate = 1 ÷ (1 + reward-to-risk ratio). For 1:2, that's about 33.3%.
lessons/trading-system-u2-l1/steps/6/pro: Your system's risk-to-reward ratio is 1:3. Ignoring costs, what's the minimum win rate to break even?
lessons/trading-system-u2-l1/steps/6/exp: 1 ÷ (1 + 3) = 25%. Check it: 0.25 × 3R − 0.75 × 1R = 0. Above 25%, expectancy turns positive.
lessons/trading-system-u2-l1/steps/7/exp: The winners' share minus the losers' share, each multiplied by its average size.
lessons/trading-system-u2-l1/steps/8/pro: Your system's win rate is 35%. Each win averages 2.5R and each loss 1R. What's the expectancy in R?
lessons/trading-system-u2-l1/steps/8/exp: (0.35 × 2.5) − (0.65 × 1) = 0.875 − 0.65 = +0.225R. Even though most trades lose, the system has a positive edge.
lessons/trading-system-u2-l2/steps/0/bod: **Drawdown** is how far your account drops from its **previous highest point** (the equity peak) to the next low, as a percentage. The biggest one is called the **max drawdown**.
lessons/trading-system-u2-l2/steps/1/pro: Your account hit a peak of $20,000 and then dropped to $17,000. What's the drawdown in percent?
lessons/trading-system-u2-l2/steps/1/exp: 3,000 ÷ 20,000 = 15%. Drawdown is measured against the peak, not the low (which would give 17.6%).
lessons/trading-system-u2-l2/steps/2/sta: Drawdown is measured from the account's starting capital, not from the previous peak.
lessons/trading-system-u2-l2/steps/2/exp: Drawdown is always measured from the previous highest point. If you grow from 10,000 to 15,000 and fall back to 12,000, that's a 20% drawdown, even though you're still above your starting capital.
lessons/trading-system-u2-l2/steps/3/pro: This chart is an account's equity curve (each candle is one week). Tap the candle that made the low of the biggest drawdown.
lessons/trading-system-u2-l2/steps/3/exp: From the peak around 12,000 to this low around 10,300 is a drop of about 14%. The second drop (from 13,400 to 12,100) was about 10%. The first candle is lower, but there was no peak before it to drop from.
lessons/trading-system-u2-l2/steps/4/bod: Even a good system has **losing streaks**. With a 50% win rate, the chance of seeing **5 losses in a row** at least once in 100 trades is about **80%**. So pick a risk per trade that a bad streak can't knock your account out with.
lessons/trading-system-u2-l2/steps/5/pro: You risk 1% of your current balance on each trade. After 10 losses in a row, roughly how much has the account dropped?
lessons/trading-system-u2-l2/steps/5/exp: Each loss multiplies the account by 0.99: 0.99 to the power of 10 ≈ 0.904, a drop of about 9.6%. With small risk, even a 10-loss streak is survivable.
lessons/trading-system-u2-l2/steps/6/pro: The account balance changed in this order. What's the max drawdown?
lessons/trading-system-u2-l2/steps/6/exp: First drop: 1,650 ÷ 11,000 = 15%. Second drop: 1,200 ÷ 12,000 = 10%. The bigger one, 15%, is the max drawdown. (6.5% comes from wrongly measuring against the starting capital.)
lessons/trading-system-u2-l2/steps/7/sen: Drawdown is measured from the previous equity ___ down to the next ___.
lessons/trading-system-u2-l2/steps/7/exp: The starting point is always the highest balance so far, not the money you first put in.
lessons/trading-system-u2-l2/steps/8/pro: Your system's backtest showed a 12% max drawdown. Which expectation is more realistic?
lessons/trading-system-u2-l2/steps/8/opt: In live trading, you may see an even bigger drawdown
Live drawdown will never go above 12%
The backtest is positive, so you won't see any drawdown
lessons/trading-system-u2-l2/steps/8/exp: A backtest is just one path through the past, and the worst stretch ahead could be worse. Many traders prepare for a drawdown around 1.5 to 2 times the backtest's.
lessons/trading-system-u2-l3/steps/0/bod: **Profit factor = total wins ÷ total losses.** Above 1 means the system made money overall, below 1 means it lost. Many traders see a profit factor above about 1.5 in a backtest as a good sign.
lessons/trading-system-u2-l3/steps/1/pro: A system's total wins are $9,000 and its total losses are $6,000. What's the profit factor?
lessons/trading-system-u2-l3/steps/1/exp: 9,000 ÷ 6,000 = 1.5. So for every $1 lost, $1.50 was made. (3,000 is the net profit, not the profit factor.)
lessons/trading-system-u2-l3/steps/2/bod: You can also get profit factor from counts and averages: **(number of wins × average win) ÷ (number of losses × average loss)**. For example, 40 wins × 250 = 10,000 and 60 losses × 100 = 6,000, so the profit factor is about 1.67.
lessons/trading-system-u2-l3/steps/3/pro: Over 20 trades, you had 8 wins averaging $300 and 12 losses averaging $150. What's the profit factor?
lessons/trading-system-u2-l3/steps/3/exp: Total wins: 8 × 300 = 2,400. Total losses: 12 × 150 = 1,800. 2,400 ÷ 1,800 ≈ 1.33. (2 is just the average win over the average loss, which ignores the counts.)
lessons/trading-system-u2-l3/steps/4/pro: With those same 20 trades ($2,400 total wins and $1,800 total losses), what's the expectancy per trade?
lessons/trading-system-u2-l3/steps/4/exp: $600 net profit ÷ 20 trades = +$30. The formula agrees: 0.4 × 300 − 0.6 × 150 = 120 − 90 = 30.
lessons/trading-system-u2-l3/steps/5/sta: A profit factor of 0.8 means the system lost money overall.
lessons/trading-system-u2-l3/steps/5/exp: Below 1 means total losses were bigger than total wins, like $8,000 in wins against $10,000 in losses.
lessons/trading-system-u2-l3/steps/6/pro: Which backtest result is more reliable?
lessons/trading-system-u2-l3/steps/6/exp: A small sample can be pure luck. A reasonable number over lots of trades is far more reliable. And a profit factor below 1 means losing money.
lessons/trading-system-u2-l3/steps/7/pai: Average profit or loss per trade
Drop from equity peak to the next low
lessons/trading-system-u2-l3/steps/8/pro: Look at this system's stats. Which conclusion is right?
lessons/trading-system-u2-l3/steps/8/opt: It loses money despite the high win rate and needs a review
A 60% win rate means the system is great
With 200 trades, it'll turn profitable eventually
When win rate is high, drawdown doesn't matter
lessons/trading-system-u2-l3/steps/8/exp: A profit factor below 1 over 200 trades means the small wins didn't cover the bigger losses. And a 35% drawdown shows how painful that ride is.
